title: Exchange Hotel, east side of Main Street
description: The Exchange Hotel was built in 1866 with a livery stable and served travellers arriving by steamboat and train. In 1908, Worden Frank Thornton bought the hotel from D. T. Day, who kept the livery business. The hotel had 20 guest rooms, an office, a writing room, a parlor, and a dining room for 40 people. In 1919, Thornton added big front windows, opened a fruit and candy store, and made the dining room into an ice cream parlor. G. A. Day later bought and renamed it the Days Inn, running it as a hotel and restaurant. After a 1933 fire, the building was rebuilt. In 1946, Gordon R. Miller opened a tearoom and soda fountain, and rented a space to Ike Hovey’s barbershop. The building burned again in 1953, and the Assembly of God Church later bought the lot.
